ar-d15651f8.stem: What happens during the locking of the knee in full extension (screw-home) with the foot on the ground?
options: The femur rotates laterally on the tibia
The tibia rotates medially on the femur
The femur rotates medially on the tibia
The patella slides upwards and locks
ar-d15651f8.explanation: Because the medial femoral condyle is longer, in the last degrees of extension in a closed chain the femur rotates medially and locks the joint; in an open chain the same movement appears as lateral rotation of the tibia. Popliteus unlocks it by rotating the femur laterally.

ar-dec32412.stem: Which statement about the suprapatellar bursa is true?
options: It is always separate from the joint cavity
It lies between the patella and the skin
It lies between the patellar ligament and the tibia
It usually communicates with the knee joint cavity and swells with joint fluid
It lies beneath the pes anserinus
ar-dec32412.explanation: The suprapatellar bursa lies beneath the quadriceps tendon in front of the femur and is like an upward extension of the joint cavity; in an effusion it swells above the patella. The prepatellar bursa lies in front of the patella, the deep infrapatellar bursa behind the patellar ligament.
notes: This describes the deep infrapatellar bursa.
This describes the pes anserinus bursa.

ar-bbea335b.stem: Which part of the menisci has no blood supply, so that tears heal poorly?
options: The ends of the posterior horns attached to the tibia
The edges attached to the capsule
The ends of the anterior horns attached to the tibia
The inner 2/3 facing into the joint (white zone)
The outer 1/3 near the capsule (red zone)
ar-bbea335b.explanation: The menisci are supplied peripherally by the perimeniscal capillary plexus; the outer third (red zone) is well vascularised and can be repaired, while the inner parts are nourished by diffusion from synovial fluid and their tears are usually resected.

ar-635bed39.stem: A footballer feels sudden pain while twisting with the knee bent and foot planted. The next day he describes tenderness along the medial joint line and occasional catching and locking; McMurray's test is positive. What is the most likely injury?
ar-635bed39.explanation: A loaded knee in flexion and rotation traps the meniscus between femur and tibia; joint-line tenderness, locking and McMurray's test suggest a meniscal tear. The medial meniscus, attached to the capsule and medial collateral ligament, is less mobile and tears more often.

ar-a84a64ee.stem: What is the most stable (close-packed) position of the hip joint?
ar-a84a64ee.explanation: In extension and internal rotation the iliofemoral, pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments tighten spirally and press the femoral head firmly into the acetabulum. Flexion–adduction–internal rotation is the position most prone to posterior dislocation (dashboard injury).

ar-21f160b4.stem: Which fibrocartilaginous ring deepens the acetabulum?
options: Ligament of the head of the femur
ar-21f160b4.explanation: The acetabular labrum attaches to the rim of the acetabulum, its lower notch completed by the transverse acetabular ligament; it deepens the joint and holds the femoral head like a suction seal. It can tear in femoroacetabular impingement.

ar-2025bf01.stem: Which statement about the medial (deltoid) ligament of the ankle is true?
options: It consists of three separate bands and is the ligament most often torn
It fans out from the medial malleolus to the talus, calcaneus and navicular; it limits eversion
It runs between the tibia and fibula
It arises from the lateral malleolus
ar-2025bf01.explanation: The deltoid ligament is very strong; in forced eversion it often avulses the medial malleolus rather than tearing. The lateral ligament complex (ATFL, CFL, PTFL) is the structure most often injured in inversion sprains.

ar-029aa2f6.explanation: The Lisfranc joint lies between the cuneiforms and cuboid and the metatarsal bases; the base of the 2nd metatarsal locks into the middle cuneiform and is the keystone of the joint. The talonavicular and calcaneocuboid joints together form the Chopart (transverse tarsal) joint.

ar-cbb80467.stem: What is the 'windlass' mechanism of the plantar fascia?
options: Dorsiflexion of the big toe tightens the plantar fascia and raises the medial arch
The fascia relaxes only when standing
The fascia tears and reattaches at heel strike
Plantarflexion of the big toe raises the arch
Ankle plantarflexion relaxes the fascia and flattens the arch
ar-cbb80467.explanation: The plantar fascia runs from the calcaneus to the bases of the toes; in push-off, when the big toe dorsiflexes, the fascia winds like a rope around the MTP joint, draws the heel and metatarsal heads together and raises the arch. The pain of the first morning steps in plantar fasciitis relates to this tension.

ar-9cae36b7.stem: What does the plantar calcaneonavicular ('spring') ligament support?
options: The lower end of the fibula
The head of the talus and the medial longitudinal arch
ar-9cae36b7.explanation: The spring ligament runs from the sustentaculum tali to the navicular and forms the floor of the socket in which the head of the talus sits; with the tibialis posterior tendon passing beneath it, it is the key support of the medial arch. Its laxity lets the head of the talus sink and causes flat foot.

ar-9dffdcc7.stem: What type of joint is the distal tibiofibular joint?
ar-9dffdcc7.explanation: The distal tibiofibular joint is a fibrous joint held by strong ligaments (anterior and posterior tibiofibular ligaments, interosseous ligament) and maintains the integrity of the ankle mortise. The proximal tibiofibular joint is a plane synovial joint.

ar-2170c9e2.stem: A patient with an ankle sprain has tenderness and swelling over the medial malleolus; the ankle X-ray shows no fracture, but he also reports pain at the upper end of the fibula just below the knee. X-ray shows a proximal fibular fracture and widening of the tibiofibular space. What is this condition called?
ar-2170c9e2.explanation: An external rotation force tears the deltoid ligament (or medial malleolus), travels up through the tibiofibular syndesmosis and interosseous membrane and fractures the proximal fibula. This is why the fibular head should never be left unexamined in ankle injuries.

ar-59f5af67.stem: Which ligament holds the sacroiliac joint together most strongly?
ar-59f5af67.explanation: The interosseous sacroiliac ligaments are short, very strong fibres behind the joint filling the space between the sacrum and the iliac tuberosity; they transfer body weight from the sacrum to the ilium. The anterior ligament is thin; the sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments are accessory ligaments that stop the sacrum tipping forwards.

ar-0814aea8.stem: Which of the following does NOT form part of the boundary of the pelvic outlet?
ar-0814aea8.explanation: The pelvic outlet is bounded in front by the pubic arch and lower border of the symphysis, at the sides by the ischial tuberosities and sacrotuberous ligaments, and behind by the tip of the coccyx. The promontory is the posterior boundary of the pelvic inlet.
